description:
We are a team from Ogbomoso, Nigeria, building a tool that helps people check a piece of land before they build or rent there.

Many families in Nigeria buy land without knowing if it floods, if water is hard to find, or if a dumpsite, quarry or fuel depot nearby could affect their health. Our app uses NASA Earth data to show how a location has changed since 1981 (rainfall, heat, wetness and fires), whether those trends are significant, and what that means for the people who will live there.
summary:
GIDEON is a web app that helps people in Nigeria check a piece of land before they build, buy, rent or farm there. Users search or tap any location and get the history of that place, its current risks and practical advice for living there safely.

To address the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective" challenge, GIDEON pulls NASA POWER climate data since 1981 (rainfall, heavy-rain days, maximum temperature and hot days) and NASA FIRMS fire records. It shows what is changing, where and by how much, and uses Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope tests to say whether each change is statistically significant. It combines these trends with elevation, nearby streams and soil data into a five-factor risk summary covering flood, heat, fire, ground stability and water, tailored to whether the user wants to build a home, farm, rent or run a business.

This matters because many families make the biggest investment of their lives without knowing whether the land floods, runs dry or overheats. GIDEON turns decades of NASA data into clear decisions that protect their health, money and safety.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

GIDEON is a web app that screens a piece of land before someone builds, buys, rents, farms or starts a business there. The user searches a place in Nigeria or taps the map to pin a plot. GIDEON then:

1. Pulls NASA POWER daily climate data for that location from 1981 to today and builds yearly records of total rainfall, heavy-rain days (over 50 mm), average maximum temperature and hot days (over 35 °C).

2. Runs Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope trend tests on each record, shows the change per decade, and labels each trend "Real trend" or "Could be chance", with a plain-language "What this means" line.

3. Checks flood exposure by comparing the plot's elevation with eight points in a 300 m ring around it (Open-Meteo) and finding the nearest stream (OpenStreetMap).

4. Checks fire activity using NASA FIRMS hotspots within 5 km, including peak burning months.

5. Checks ground stability from soil clay, sand and organic carbon (ISRIC SoilGrids) and slope.

6. Checks water availability from dry-season length and its trend, and shows nearby local water quality reports, clearly labelled as local data, not satellite data.

7. Combines everything into a five-factor risk summary (flood, heat, fire, ground, water), tailored to the user's goal: Build Home, Farmland, Rent Property or Commercial.

Users can compare two locations, share a report, and read results in English, Yoruba or Pidgin. An offline demo mode with three Ogbomoso locations keeps it working without internet.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Many Nigerian families spend their life savings on land without knowing whether it floods, overheats or runs dry. GIDEON gives them that knowledge in seconds, for free. It helps them avoid unsafe plots, plan protective measures (raised floors, drainage, deeper boreholes, ventilation, water treatment), and ask better questions before paying. Over time, we want it to support estate agents, surveyors, farmers and local governments in planning safer communities.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

- Built with Google AI Studio and Gemini [confirm: React / TypeScript]

- Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for mapping

- [Chart library, e.g. Recharts] for trend charts

- Data: NASA POWER, NASA FIRMS, Open-Meteo elevation API, OpenStreetMap Overpass API, ISRIC SoilGrids, and local water reports

- Trend statistics (Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope) written in code

CREATIVITY

GIDEON turns abstract NASA climate records into a decision a family can act on. Instead of showing raw data, it answers personal questions: "Will this land flood?" "Will my borehole run dry?" The same location gives different priorities depending on whether the user wants to build, farm, rent or run a business. Local languages and offline demo mode make it practical for Nigerian users with limited data access.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Honesty about limits: satellite grids (about 50 km) describe the wider area, not the exact plot, and water contamination cannot be seen from space. The app says so and always advises a surveyor, soil engineer and water test.

- Statistical rigour: trends are only called "real" when they are statistically significant.

- Accessibility: plain language, local languages, works on mobile, works offline in demo mode.

- Health: water safety, heat and smoke exposure are framed around family health, guided by a registered nurse on our team.
